form.title: gemini frigivelse summary for QP
form.what: Gemini (google workspace) reads the batchjournal review comments, the open deviations, the EM summary and the CoA from LIMS and writes a 1 page release summary that ends with 'batch can be certified: YES/NO + reason'. QP reads it before certifying. saves the QP about 1 hour per batch

gmp_impact.explain: the QP makes the decision, not the AI

form.who_checks: QP, every batch

source.explain: google workspace licence we already have

rationale: The output ends in a proposed certification conclusion (YES/NO + reason), i.e. an input to batch certification, a GMP decision. Guide §2 counts 'provides input to a GMP decision' as critical and keeps human review in autonomy; A22 §1 says LLMs should not be used in critical applications, HITL does not rescue that. Other reading: if Gemini only collated the facts and the QP works from the source records, it is non_critical summarising -> permitted_with_hitl. The explicit yes/no recommendation tips it to critical. The proposer ticked 'no' because the QP signs (self-assessment).

form.title: AP invoice matching
form.what: Finance wants the SAP add-on that matches supplier invoices to POs and goods receipts with machine learning and posts the ones it is confident about. The rest go to the AP clerk. It's only about paying invoices, nothing to do with material release.

ai_type.explain: vendor says it is trained on our last 3 years of invoices

output_use.explain: AP team checks exceptions and a weekly sample

form.who_checks: AP team lead, weekly sample of 20 postings

rationale: Accounts payable is a business function outside GMP-regulated activities; the form states explicitly that material release is not touched. Model type and autonomy do not change the outcome.

form.title: Flow imaging particle classification for release testing
form.what: QC wants to use the vendor's ML classifier for flow imaging microscopy (MFI) images. It classifies sub-visible particles in drug product as protein aggregate, silicone oil droplet, air bubble or other. The particle counts per class are reported as the release result for sub-visible particles. The model version is fixed by the vendor and installed with the instrument software.

gmp_impact.explain: the counts are the reported release result

ai_type.explain: CNN, locked version, we would validate it

output_use.explain: results go to LIMS, analyst reviews the run report and second-person review as normal

form.who_checks: Analyst reviews the run report, a second analyst reviews as part of normal data review. Images are kept.

rationale: The model's classification produces a QC release result (critical) and is a locked, trained model (static). Individual particle classifications are not reviewed, only the run report, so acts_with_oversight; the verdict is annex22_full whatever the autonomy level.

form.title: AI for QC
form.what: manager came back from a conference and wants 'AI in the QC lab' this year. not sure yet what exactly, maybe something with the results or the planning. want to know what is allowed

rationale: A proposed AI use in a GMP area, so in scope, but neither the task (results vs planning) nor the model type is known. gmp_relevance and model_type unclear -> needs_more_information.

form.title: Copilot writes monthly quality KPI narrative
form.what: Every month QA compiles the quality KPIs (deviations opened/closed, CAPA overdue, right first time, complaints) for management review. we want copilot to take the power bi export and write the narrative + 'key messages' and publish it straight to the management review sharepoint page. no one has time to proof read it, managers just read it in the meeting

gmp_impact.explain: it's just a report, the numbers come from power bi

form.who_checks: nobody before publishing. if a manager sees something odd they can ask

rationale: Management review of quality KPIs is a PQS activity, so GMP context; the narrative does not decide anything and is not a batch record -> non_critical. It is published with no review -> acts_autonomously -> hitl_required (A22 §1 HITL for non-critical LLM use). Other reading: a management report is generic office productivity (not_gmp -> outside_gmp). Chosen non_critical because the 'key messages' steer quality decisions in the PQS.

form.title: question
form.what: whats the difference between a static and a dynamic model in annex 22? need it for a slide tomorrow

rationale: General knowledge question about the guideline; no use case to screen.

form.title: RPA bot for supplier CoA entry
form.what: The incoming QC team retypes supplier CoA values (pH, endotoxin, bioburden) for media and buffer components into SAP QM. IT built a UiPath bot that reads the supplier portal and fills the inspection lot fields. It uses fixed screen-scraping rules; the 'AI' in the project name is marketing from IT.

gmp_impact.explain: the values are used for the usage decision of the raw material

output_use.explain: QC checks before the usage decision

form.who_checks: QC raw material reviewer compares against the CoA pdf for 1 in 10 lots

rationale: Explicitly programmed RPA, nothing learned from data, so A22 does not apply (A22 §1 covers models that obtained functionality through training). It writes GMP data used for material release, so it is a critical computerised system under Annex 11 (data integrity, validation).

form.title: chatgpt enterprise for CAPA drafts
form.what: investigators struggle to write good CAPA actions and effectiveness checks. idea: paste the root cause from the eQMS into ChatGPT Enterprise, it suggests 3-5 CAPA actions and an effectiveness check plan, the investigator picks/edits and enters them in the eQMS where QA approves as usual

gmp_impact.explain: the investigator writes the final CAPA and QA approves

form.who_checks: investigator edits, QA approves the CAPA in the eQMS like today

rationale: Drafting support: the CAPA that counts is written by the investigator and approved by QA in the normal process. The LLM does not classify, disposition or decide anything. non_critical + generative + reviewed -> permitted_with_hitl.

form.title: LLM decides chrom pooling
form.what: DSP idea from a vendor demo: an LLM agent reads the UV trace and the fraction table from the chromatography software export after the CEX step and tells the operator which fractions to pool, using the pooling criteria in the MBR. Would save calling MSAT at 3 am. The demo used GPT-4o and the sales guy said the licence is cheap if we sign before December.

ai_type.explain: GPT-4o via the vendor's agent platform

form.who_checks: operator does the pooling as the agent says, MSAT looks at it the next morning

rationale: Fraction pooling is an in-process decision that sets product purity: critical. An LLM makes it -> not permitted (A22 §1). The 'informs' tick contradicts the free text (operator pools as told, MSAT reviews afterwards), so autonomy is acts_with_oversight; the verdict does not depend on it.

form.title: HPLC column end-of-life prediction
form.what: We have years of system suitability data (plate count, tailing, back pressure) per HPLC/UPLC column. A data scientist trained a random forest that predicts how many injections a column has left so we can order and qualify replacement columns in time. Frozen model, retrained only via change request. System suitability still decides whether a run is valid; the prediction does not.

gmp_impact.explain: only for ordering and planning; SST decides validity

form.who_checks: Lab supervisor looks at it when planning column orders

rationale: Planning support in the QC lab; run validity is still decided by system suitability, so the output is not a GMP decision -> non_critical, static -> permitted_risk_based.

form.title: inspection observation about chatgpt
form.what: During last month's inspection the inspector saw that we used ChatGPT to draft some SOPs last year (all were reviewed and approved through doc control, I checked). They wrote it up as an observation. Can they fine us for this? And what exactly should we write in the response so it goes away? Our consultant says it is nothing but my boss is nervous and the client heard about it too.

rationale: The request is for legal consequences and wording of an inspection response, i.e. legal advice / a compliance verdict (guide §1). The past ChatGPT drafting could be screened on its own form, but that is not what is asked.

form.title: ML extends calibration intervals in CMMS
form.what: Engineering wants a model trained on 6 years of calibration as-found/as-left data for pressure, temperature and flow transmitters (bioreactors, WFI loop, autoclaves). It predicts drift and sets the next calibration due date in the CMMS automatically, extending intervals for stable instruments up to 2x. The model is frozen after training; we would retrain once a year under change control. Saves around 30% of calibration hours, the business case is already with the site director.
form.who_checks: metrology lead gets a monthly list of the intervals that were changed and can override

rationale: Calibration intervals of GMP instruments are a control that assures the reliability of process and sterilisation measurements; the model sets them directly in the CMMS -> critical (input to/acting on a GMP control). Other reading: maintenance planning support (non_critical -> permitted_risk_based), as the proposer thinks. 'informs' contradicts 'sets the next due date automatically'; the free text wins -> acts_with_oversight (monthly list, override). Static -> annex22_full.

form.title: linkedin posts w/ gemini
form.what: marketing wants Gemini to write our linkedin posts and make images for the trade show booth. posts go out after the marketing manager ok's them. nothing with batches
form.who_checks: marketing manager

rationale: Marketing is outside GMP. AI Act Art. 50 transparency on AI-generated images is a side note, not a GMP outcome.

form.title: New bioreactor controller with 'AI feed optimisation'
form.what: The bioreactor supplier offers a software upgrade for the 2000 L SUBs with 'AI feed optimisation'. It changes the glucose/feed rate during the run based on the online sensors. The sales rep said it 'uses machine learning' and 'improves over time', but the technical datasheet says the model is fixed per software release. We have asked for clarification, no answer yet.

gmp_impact.explain: it changes the feed during GMP runs

form.who_checks: operators and shift lead watch trends, alarms as usual

rationale: Feed control is a process control -> critical. Model type is genuinely unknown: 'improves over time' means dynamic (-> not_permitted_critical), 'fixed per release' means static (-> annex22_full). The two readings give different outcomes, so model_type unclear -> needs_more_information until the supplier documentation (A22 §2.2) settles it.

form.title: EMS 'AI alarm' module
form.what: our EM system (particle counters, room dP, temp/RH in grade A-D) vendor sold us an 'AI smart alarm' add-on. after asking, it turns out it's rate-of-change and persistence rules we configure ourselves, e.g. alarm if dP drops >5 Pa in 30 s or particles above alert for 3 consecutive samples. nothing is trained

ai_type.explain: vendor calls it AI, see description

output_use.explain: alarms go to the control room

form.who_checks: control room operator acknowledges alarms, EM team reviews the alarm log weekly

rationale: Grade A/B alarms are critical. The tick 'supplier AI feature, details unknown' suggests model_type unclear (-> needs_more_information), but the free text establishes configured fixed rules, nothing trained -> non_ml -> Annex 11 (alarm settings, §8) and not Annex 22.

form.title: Claude for root cause brainstorming
form.what: During deviation investigations the investigator would paste the event description and the timeline into Claude (company account) and ask for possible root causes and a fishbone. The investigator uses it as a brainstorm partner; the root cause in the report is written and justified by the investigator with evidence. Classification and batch impact are done by QA as today, not by the AI.

gmp_impact.explain: it helps the investigation but doesn't decide

form.who_checks: investigator + QA approver of the deviation report

rationale: Reading 1 (chosen): brainstorming support; root cause, classification and batch impact stay with the investigator and QA, so the output is not itself a GMP decision -> non_critical -> permitted_with_hitl. Reading 2: root cause feeds the deviation outcome and CAPA, so it is input to a GMP decision -> critical -> not_permitted_critical. Chosen non_critical because classification and disposition are explicitly excluded and the investigator must justify the root cause with evidence.

form.title: weekly TT status mail to clients
form.what: MSAT project managers spend friday afternoons writing status updates for each client tech transfer. plan: copilot reads the project tracker, the open action list and the last meeting minutes and writes the weekly update email. the email goes to the client contact automatically friday 3pm so PMs don't have to remember

gmp_impact.explain: just project status, no batch data

form.who_checks: the PM is in cc so they see what was sent

rationale: The tick says a person approves, but the free text describes automatic sending with the PM only in cc, i.e. no review before the output takes effect -> acts_autonomously -> hitl_required. Read by the tick it would be permitted_with_hitl. Tech-transfer communication with the contract giver is GMP context but not a GMP decision -> non_critical (some would call it not_gmp project admin).

form.title: Headspace CCI accept/reject with ML
form.what: For the lyophilised vials we use laser headspace analysis for 100% container closure integrity testing on the line. The new vendor software version replaces the fixed threshold with a trained classifier (trained on our leak/no-leak reference vials, locked version). Vials classified as leaking are rejected automatically by the line.
form.who_checks: QA reviews reject rates per batch; a challenge set of known leakers is run at the start of each batch

rationale: Accept/reject of individual vials for container closure integrity is critical; the classifier is trained and locked -> static -> annex22_full.

form.title: summarize
form.what: can u summarise annex 1 in 10 bullets pls

rationale: A summarisation request for a guideline; no AI use case to screen.

form.title: AI trending for CPV
form.what: MSAT runs continued process verification for 6 commercial products. A python script pulls CQAs and CPPs from the historian and LIMS, calculates control limits and flags Nelson rule violations; the flags go into the quarterly CPV report. We call it the 'AI trending tool' internally but it is just statistics, no machine learning.

gmp_impact.explain: the CPV report is a GMP document and signals can trigger deviations

output_use.explain: MSAT engineer reviews the flags before the report

form.who_checks: MSAT engineer reviews every flag, QA approves the CPV report

rationale: The tick 'trained prediction model' contradicts the description (statistical control limits and Nelson rules, no ML). Guide §3 puts SPC limits under non_ml -> Annex 11, not Annex 22. Read by the tick it would be static -> annex22_full. Criticality does not change the outcome here (signals feed GMP trending and deviations, labelled critical).

form.title: LLM vurderer change control impact
form.what: In change control the kvalitetsafdeling spends a lot of time on impact assessments. We want the LLM in the eQMS (the vendor's new 'AI assistant', runs on Azure OpenAI) to read the change description and propose the change classification (minor/major/critical), whether revalidation is needed, and whether the client and the authorities must be notified. QA confirms or changes it before the CR moves on.
form.who_checks: QA change control coordinator, for every CR

rationale: The LLM proposes the change classification, the revalidation need and regulatory/client notification: these are GMP decisions, comparable to the guide's 'classifying deviation criticality' example -> critical; HITL does not change criticality (guide §2) -> not_permitted_critical. Other reading: an assessment draft that QA approves in the normal process (non_critical -> permitted_with_hitl). Chosen critical because the output is the classification itself, not a draft text.

form.title: contract review copilot
form.what: Legal wants Copilot (with its contract review plugin) to check incoming master service agreements and NDAs from new clients against our contract playbook: liability caps, payment terms, IP, governing law. It marks deviations from the playbook and suggests redlines. The quality agreement is a separate document negotiated by QA and is NOT part of this.

output_use.explain: the lawyer decides on each redline

form.who_checks: the responsible lawyer

rationale: Contracts with contract givers underpin outsourced GMP activities (EU GMP Chapter 7), so one could argue GMP context (non_critical -> permitted_with_hitl). But the form explicitly excludes the quality agreement; liability, payment and IP terms are legal/commercial -> not_gmp -> outside_gmp.

form.title: chatgpt to answer client complaints
form.what: Clients send quality complaints (damaged shipper, missing CoA page, particles seen at the client's site). The complaint handler would use ChatGPT to write the first response letter and the acknowledgement. the investigation itself stays in the eQMS.

rationale: Complaint handling is GMP context; the letter is not the investigation or a disposition -> non_critical generative. Whether anyone reads the letter before it goes out is open ('depends on workload', who_checks blank). If reviewed -> permitted_with_hitl, if sent unreviewed -> hitl_required; since the gap changes the outcome, autonomy unclear -> needs_more_information. Other reading: assume the handler obviously sends it himself (permitted_with_hitl). Client data into a free ChatGPT account is a separate data-policy flag.

form.title: predict filter clogging in media prep
form.what: media prep: depth/sterile filtration of cell culture media sometimes clogs halfway and we lose time changing filters. a trained model (frozen) on 2 yrs of pressure/flow data predicts minutes until clogging and shows it on the HMI so the operator can get a spare filter ready. it does not change anything in the process, the filter integrity test is done as usual

rationale: Operational information only: the model shows a clogging estimate, the operator decides, process settings and filter integrity testing are unchanged -> non_critical. output_use is blank but the description shows informs. Static -> permitted_risk_based.

form.title: copilot for EM excursion impact assessments
form.what: When an EM action limit excursion happens in grade A/B, micro writes an afvigelse with the impact assessment. We want Copilot to pull the EM results, the identification and the batch that was filled, write the impact assessment and the conclusion 'no impact on product' / 'impact' into the deviation in the eQMS and close it if there is no impact. This would clear our backlog of 40 open EM deviations
form.who_checks: micro lead gets a notification when the deviation is closed

rationale: The impact conclusion on a grade A/B excursion drives batch disposition and becomes the GMP record -> critical; an LLM -> not permitted. 'person approves' contradicts the free text (closed automatically, notification afterwards) -> acts_autonomously; the verdict is the same either way.

form.title: trained classifier proposes deviation class
form.what: Our data science team fine-tuned a BERT model (it is a 'language model' but it only classifies, it does not write any text) on 8 years of closed deviations to propose minor/major/critical when a deviation is opened. The model is frozen and versioned, same input gives the same class. QA reviews and sets the final class.

gmp_impact.explain: classification drives investigation depth and batch disposition

form.who_checks: QA deviation coordinator, every deviation

rationale: Deviation classification driving disposition is a guide example of critical. The contested point is model type: BERT is a 'language model', so some would treat it as LLM/generative (-> not_permitted_critical). As described it is a frozen, deterministic encoder classifier that produces a class, not generated text -> static -> annex22_full, with A22 §3.3/§10.5 HITL records.

form.title: reg intel nyhedsbrev
form.what: RA monitors EMA, FDA, PIC/S and Laegemiddelstyrelsen publications. Gemini would summarise new guidelines and consultation documents each week into a nyhedsbrev for RA and QA, with links to the originals. Anyone who acts on something reads the original.
form.who_checks: RA specialist skims the newsletter before sending

rationale: Summarising guidance for QA/RA is the guide's example of non_critical (GMP context, supports people who work through the normal process). Other reading: public regulatory news is not a GMP activity at all (not_gmp -> outside_gmp). Chosen non_critical because QA uses it to keep the PQS current. Informs + an RA skim -> permitted_with_hitl.

form.title: Annex 22 statement for audit binder
form.what: We validated our AI visual inspection last year, big project, 14 months, the vendor was great and the validation report is 300 pages. A client auditor comes on Monday and last time they asked a lot about AI. Can this tool issue a statement that our system is Annex 22 compliant, ideally signed or with a logo, so I can put it in the audit binder? We don't have time to re-read everything before Monday and my manager is on holiday.

rationale: A request for a formal compliance statement (final verdict) for an auditor, explicitly out of scope per guide §1, even though an AI system is mentioned.

form.title: LLM auto-tags documents in eDMS
form.what: Document control wants the LLM feature in our eDMS (uses OpenAI) to read every new or revised SOP, form and work instruction and fill in the metadata: keywords, related equipment, related processes and a 2-line abstract shown in the search results. doc control doesn't have time to check 300 docs a month. the document content itself is not changed, approval flow unchanged
form.who_checks: nobody, it writes the tags automatically when the doc is released; users will report wrong tags

rationale: Gmp: the abstract and tags are search aids, the approved document is unchanged -> non_critical; another reading is that wrong 'related equipment' metadata in a validated eDMS can make users miss an applicable SOP (data integrity of GMP records, critical). Autonomy: the 'informs' tick contradicts 'writes the tags automatically, nobody checks' -> acts_autonomously. non_critical + generative + no HITL -> hitl_required.

form.title: self-learning forecast of clean steam / WFI demand
form.what: The utilities team wants a forecasting tool that predicts WFI and clean steam demand for the next 48 h from the production schedule and CIP/SIP plans, so we can plan still and generator runs and avoid running out of WFI during CIP. It retrains automatically every night on yesterday's consumption. It does not control the WFI system; operators decide when to start the stills. WFI quality is monitored by the normal TOC/conductivity and micro sampling.

output_use.explain: forecast shown on the utilities dashboard

form.who_checks: utilities operator uses it for planning

source.explain: part of the utilities SCADA package

rationale: Planning support for a GMP utility; it does not control the system and WFI quality is assured by the normal monitoring -> non_critical. Dynamic models are excluded only from critical uses (A22 §1) -> permitted_risk_based, with risk-based controls on the nightly retraining.

form.title: Copilot for MSAT data
form.what: MSAT wants Copilot to 'analyse process data' faster. They would upload exports from the historian and ask things like 'why was titer low in batch X' or 'compare these runs'. Not decided yet what the answers are used for: maybe investigations, maybe client reports, maybe just curiosity.

gmp_impact.explain: depends what it ends up being used for

form.who_checks: the engineer

rationale: The intended use is not defined (A22 §3.1): as curiosity or exploratory support it is non_critical -> permitted_with_hitl; feeding deviation investigations or client batch reports could make it input to GMP decisions/records (critical -> not_permitted_critical). gmp_relevance unclear -> needs_more_information. Other reading: 'informs' + engineer reviews is enough to call it non_critical.

form.title: vision system label check 'AI'
form.what: On the labelling line the camera checks that the printed batch number and expiry date on each vial label are correct and readable. The supplier's new version uses 'deep learning OCR'. I don't know the details; their sales sheet says 'AI-based, trained at the factory, no learning on site, fixed model per software version'. Wrong or unreadable labels are kicked out automatically.

output_use.explain: challenge vials at line start and every hour

form.who_checks: line operator runs challenge test vials, QA reviews reject counts

rationale: Label accept/reject is critical. The tick 'details unknown' suggests model_type unclear (-> needs_more_information), but the supplier's documented statement (trained, fixed per version, no on-site learning) is enough to classify as static -> annex22_full; verifying the claim is a supplier-documentation control (A22 §2.2), not a reason to withhold the outcome.

form.title: power automate training assignment
form.what: When doc control releases a new SOP revision, a Power Automate flow looks up the SOP's training matrix in SharePoint and assigns read & understand training in the LMS to the right job roles, with a due date before the effective date. Fixed lookup rules, no AI really, but the project is part of our 'AI & automation' program so I'm filling this in.

gmp_impact.explain: training records, people must be trained before the effective date

output_use.explain: training coordinator checks the assignment report

form.who_checks: training coordinator checks the weekly assignment report

rationale: Explicitly programmed workflow, nothing learned -> non_ml; it supports the GMP training process (the LMS completion record is the record) -> Annex 11, not Annex 22.

form.title: image cell counter for seed train
form.what: For seed train passaging (shake flasks to 50 L / 200 L) the operators decide the split ratio and passage go/no-go from VCD and viability. A new image-based cell counter uses an ML segmentation model. The vendor's validation note says inference is 'stochastic (Monte Carlo sampling for uncertainty)', so the same image can give slightly different counts. They say within +/-3%.
form.who_checks: we take a sample from the flask, load the slide, it gives VCD and viability, then we calculate the split in the batch record. shift lead checks

rationale: VCD/viability used for passage go/no-go is an in-process control -> critical. The model is frozen, but its output is explicitly non-deterministic for identical inputs; A22 §1 excludes probabilistic-output models from critical use -> not_permitted_critical. Other reading: the variability is just measurement uncertainty of an analytical method, treat as static (-> annex22_full). The guide's definition is about identical inputs giving different outputs, which the vendor confirms. The who_checks field describes the process rather than the check.

form.title: operator performance score
form.what: Production management wants to use MES data (time per batch step, number of corrections, right-first-time on EBR entries) and an ML model to give each operator a monthly performance score, used in the yearly appraisal and for bonus. It would also suggest who needs more coaching.

output_use.explain: managers use it in appraisal talks

form.who_checks: line managers

rationale: Purpose is HR (appraisal, bonus); GMP data is only the input -> not_gmp -> outside_gmp. Other reading: the coaching suggestions touch GMP training (non_critical -> permitted_risk_based). The important point for the proposer is the AI Act: evaluating worker performance is high-risk under Annex III point 4(b), with deployer duties (Art. 26).

form.title: AI to write PQ summary reports
form.what: Validation engineers write the summary report after each executed PQ/PPQ protocol. We'd use Claude (enterprise) to draft the report from the executed protocol, the deviation list and the data tables. The validation lead rewrites as needed and the report goes through the normal review and approval by validation + QA in the eDMS. nothing is issued without signatures
form.who_checks: validation lead + QA approve every report in the eDMS

rationale: The tick 'takes effect automatically, spot checks' contradicts the free text: every report is reviewed and approved under document control before issue -> recommends. The approved report, not the AI draft, is the GMP record (guide §2) -> non_critical -> permitted_with_hitl. Read by the tick it would be hitl_required.

form.title: julefrokost seating
form.what: can the AI plan the seating for the julefrokost? 120 people, some of the QC people don't like sitting with production lol, and the DJ needs space near the bar

rationale: Unrelated to screening an AI use case (party planning).

form.title: LLM grades training assessments
form.what: For aseptic operator qualification, trainees answer 15 open questions after the theory module. Gemini would grade the answers against the model answers and set pass/fail directly in the LMS. Passing is one of the prerequisites before the operator can join an aseptic process simulation (media fill). Trainers can look at the scores if they want.

gmp_impact.explain: training is GMP but it's not about the batch

form.who_checks: trainers, if they want

rationale: The LLM's pass/fail becomes the GMP training record and gates access to aseptic qualification, i.e. a GMP record used as such -> critical -> not_permitted_critical. Other reading: theory grading is training support, the media fill is the real qualification gate (non_critical) -> with no review that is hitl_required. Either way not acceptable as described. Also AI Act Annex III (evaluation of learning outcomes / worker evaluation).

form.title: copliot for URS drafts
form.what: engineering writes URS for new equipment (e.g. a new 2000L SUB or a TFF skid) idea is copliot makes the first draft from our template + the vendor brochures + our old URS engineer edits then the normal review and approval (process owner QA) in the eDMS
form.who_checks: author, process owner and QA approve under doc control

rationale: First draft of a GMP document that is reviewed and approved under document control: the approved URS is the record (guide §2) -> non_critical -> permitted_with_hitl.

form.title: supplier qualification AI + warehouse
form.what: 1) Supplier quality wants a tool that reads supplier audit reports, questionnaires and CoA history and gives each supplier a risk score and approved / conditional / not approved status in the approved supplier list. we saw it at a conference, not sure what's under the hood. 2) also the warehouse asked if the same tool can help them find materials in the racks
form.who_checks: SQA manager reviews the list monthly

rationale: Two use cases; the main subject is (1), setting approved-supplier status, a GMP decision -> critical. The model type is unknown ('not sure what's under the hood'), and for a critical use it decides between annex22_full and not_permitted_critical -> needs_more_information. Use case (2) needs its own form.

form.title: Auto-replies to the Ask QA mailbox
form.what: QA gets about 60 mails a week in the 'Ask QA' mailbox: where is the SOP for X, which form do I use, can I correct this logbook entry. A Copilot Studio agent connected to the eDMS would answer these automatically and close the mail. QA would only see the mails the bot can't answer.

gmp_impact.explain: it only answers questions, people still follow the SOP

form.who_checks: no one checks the bot's answers, we might do a sample later

rationale: GMP context, the answer is guidance rather than a GMP decision -> non_critical. Autonomy is debatable: the requester is a human who acts on the answer (informs -> permitted_with_hitl), but the bot replies as the QA function and closes the request, so its answer takes effect as QA's answer with no qualified review -> acts_autonomously -> hitl_required. Chosen acts_autonomously because the proposer ticks it and QA never sees the answers.

form.title: camera checks gowning before grade B
form.what: At the entrance to the grade B filling suite a camera with a trained model (frozen, vendor trained it on our gowning photos) checks hood, goggles, mask, gloves taped, no skin visible. If it detects a gowning error the door to grade B stays locked and the operator has to re-gown. This replaces the mirror self-check. gowning qualification and glove/gown EM stay as today

gmp_impact.explain: contamination control, but the operator is still trained

form.who_checks: nobody per event; the supervisor gets a daily count of blocked entries

rationale: The model replaces an existing contamination-control step (mirror self-check) and directly controls access to grade B -> critical; a missed gowning error goes undetected. Other reading: an extra aid on top of gowning qualification and EM (non_critical -> permitted_risk_based). Chosen critical because it replaces a control, so A22 §4.3 (no decrease vs the replaced process) applies. Autonomy: the 'nobody checks' tick vs the daily count of blocked entries -> acts_with_oversight; static -> annex22_full. Employee images also need a privacy assessment.

form.title: smart weighing & dispensing
form.what: New weighing & dispensing booth software for buffer prep. Scans the material barcode, checks it against the recipe in the MES, checks expiry and status (released/quarantine), tells the operator the target weight and blocks if outside tolerance. The vendor brochure says 'AI-powered error prevention'. I asked their engineer: it's configured rules and the recipe tolerances, nothing trained.

gmp_impact.explain: wrong material or weight = wrong buffer

form.who_checks: operator + second-person verification for critical additions, batch record review

rationale: The tick 'trained prediction model' contradicts the engineer's answer (configured rules and tolerances, nothing trained). Specific free text wins -> non_ml -> Annex 11, not Annex 22. Read by the tick: critical + static -> annex22_full.

form.title: EM isolate clustering dashboard
form.what: Micro identifies EM isolates (MALDI-TOF). A frozen clustering/classification model groups isolates by species, room and time and highlights unusual clusters (e.g. the same Staph species in 3 grade C rooms within a week) on a dashboard. Micro uses it in the monthly EM trend meeting and to get ideas on contamination sources. EM limits, excursion handling and the trend report are unchanged and done by micro
form.who_checks: micro team in the monthly EM trend meeting

rationale: Guide §2 lists 'trending dashboards for information' as non_critical; limits, excursion handling and the trend report stay manual -> permitted_risk_based. Other reading: highlighted clusters steer contamination investigations, so input to GMP decisions (critical -> annex22_full). Chosen non_critical because micro still owns the trend report and excursion decisions.

form.title: annex 22 timing
form.what: is annex 22 final yet?? when does it apply and do we have to redo our CSV for old systems

rationale: General knowledge/regulatory status question; no use case described.

form.title: auto notes fra tavlemoede
form.what: every morning tier 1 board meeting on the production floor (yesterdays deviations, equipment down, staffing, safety) Teams Premium records it and Copilot makes the notes and the action list and posts them in the production channel automatically nobody edits them the actions get followed up from the notes. later we also want Copilot to write the shift handover into the logbook

rationale: Main subject: tier-1 meeting notes. Deviation and equipment actions are followed up from them, so GMP context but not a GMP record -> non_critical; posted with no review -> hitl_required. Other reading: meeting notes are generic office productivity (not_gmp -> outside_gmp). The second idea (AI-written logbook handover) would be a GMP record and needs its own form; it is not labelled here.

form.title: Gemini helps write R code for stability trending
form.what: The QC stability coordinator wants to use Gemini to help write R scripts for stability regression (shelf-life estimation per ICH Q1E) and the plots. The analyst checks the code, and the script would be verified/validated per our spreadsheet & script CSV SOP before it is used for reportable calculations.
form.who_checks: analyst + CSV verification before GMP use

rationale: The LLM is a development aid: it writes code that a person reviews and that is validated before use; the GMP calculation is then done by a deterministic script under Annex 11, never by the LLM -> non_critical -> permitted_with_hitl. Other reading (the proposer ticked 'yes'): the generated code computes shelf-life, an input to a GMP decision -> critical -> not_permitted_critical. Chosen non_critical because no LLM output is used as a GMP result.

form.title: AI to chase suppliers
form.what: Supplier quality sends annual questionnaires and chases missing certificates (ISO, TSE/BSE statements, nitrosamine statements). An LLM agent would write and send the reminder emails and summarise the answers back into our supplier file (the original documents are filed too). not decided yet if someone reads the summaries before filing
form.who_checks: not decided

rationale: Supplier qualification support in GMP context; originals are filed, so the summaries are not the record -> non_critical generative. Review of the summaries and emails is 'not decided', and it changes the outcome (permitted_with_hitl vs hitl_required) -> autonomy unclear -> needs_more_information. Other reading: 'just admin' emails could be not_gmp.

form.title: ML model ends protein A loading at predicted breakthrough
form.what: In continuous capture (periodic counter-current chromatography) we want an in-house ML model that predicts breakthrough from the inline UV and the titer, and switches the column at the predicted 1% breakthrough instead of after a fixed load volume. Trained on development and engineering runs, frozen, will be validated. The PCC controller executes the switch automatically.

gmp_impact.explain: controls column switching = load = yield and impurity clearance

output_use.explain: operators monitor UV traces, alarms on deviation

form.who_checks: DSP operators watch the run; MSAT reviews each batch's switching data

rationale: The model directly controls a process step that determines load and impurity clearance -> critical; frozen trained model -> static -> annex22_full (full validation, input sample space monitoring, change control).

form.title: phishing filter
form.what: IT security: turn on the ML phishing detection in our email gateway. quarantines suspicious mails automatically, users can request release. corporate email only
form.who_checks: IT SOC reviews the quarantine reports

rationale: Corporate IT security, not a GMP activity -> outside_gmp. The model type is unknown, but outside_gmp has priority over needs_more_information in the rules, so the gap does not matter.

form.title: GPT generates vial/carton label text
form.what: For clinical supply batches the label text (product code, batch no., expiry, storage conditions, protocol no.) per country is typed by packaging planners today. We'd let an LLM (Azure OpenAI) generate the label text per country from the batch record and the client's label spec, including translation, and send it directly to the label printing system.
form.who_checks: packaging operator does a visual check of the first printed label of each run

rationale: Label content (batch, expiry, storage) directly affects patient safety -> critical; an LLM generates it -> not_permitted_critical. 'person approves' contradicts the flow (sent straight to the printer, first-label check only) -> acts_with_oversight; the verdict does not depend on it.

form.title: predict chromatography resin lifetime for purchasing
form.what: Protein A resin is expensive. Supply chain and MSAT want a model that predicts how many cycles each resin lot will last (from cycle number, pressure, step yield, HCP clearance trend) so we can plan purchases 9 months ahead. The data scientist used a Bayesian neural network; it samples, so running it twice gives slightly different predictions with an uncertainty band. Resin reuse limits are still set by the validated lifetime study, the model doesn't change those.
form.who_checks: supply planner

rationale: Purchasing planning; reuse limits stay with the validated lifetime study -> non_critical. Model type: ticked 'trained, frozen' (static), but the output varies for identical inputs -> probabilistic per guide §3. Both readings give permitted_risk_based for a non-critical use; the probabilistic label matters only if the use ever became critical (A22 §1).

form.title: python for lims export
form.what: write me a python script that reads our LIMS csv export and plots the endotoxin results per month

rationale: A coding request to the tool itself, not a use case to screen.

form.title: CDS upgrade 'AI assistant'
form.what: The CDS vendor's next major version comes with an 'AI assistant' that is switched on by default. The release notes say it can 'help with method setup, review and reporting'. We don't know what it does exactly or what it's built on. Upgrade is planned for Q2.

rationale: 'Review and reporting' in a CDS could be critical (QC results) or merely assistive; the model type is unknown. Both unclear -> needs_more_information; supplier documentation is needed (A22 §2.2, A11D §7.4).

form.title: AI for the training team
form.what: Training team has two ideas: (a) make short scenario videos with AI avatars for the yearly GMP refresher (e.g. an 'operator' explaining a gowning mistake), script and video generated by an AI video tool from our approved SOPs; the SOP owner and the training lead review and approve every video before it goes into the LMS. (b) a fun chatbot on the intranet for the canteen menu. Mostly we want (a) approved.

ai_type.explain: AI video avatar tool + chatgpt for the scripts

form.who_checks: SOP owner + training lead approve each video

rationale: Two use cases; the main one is (a). GMP training material generated by AI and approved before use: the approved SOP stays the master -> non_critical -> permitted_with_hitl. (b) alone would be outside_gmp; a classifier that labels (b) gets gmp_relevance wrong. AI Act Art. 50 applies to synthetic video (disclose it is AI-generated).

form.title: agent answers client audit questionnaires
form.what: Ok so this is a big one for us. Every month we get 3-4 pre-audit questionnaires from prospective and existing clients (quality system, data integrity, deviation handling, supplier qualification, sometimes 200 questions). Our QA compliance team of two people can't keep up, and we lost a deal last year partly because we were slow (according to BD). We saw a demo of an AI agent that answers questionnaires from our quality manual and SOPs and uploads the answers in the client's supplier portal. Budget is approx 40k a year. Head of QA approves the answers of course. In practice the agent submits as soon as it's complete so we hit the deadline, and QA gets a copy.

ai_type.explain: AI agent, built on GPT i think

form.who_checks: QA gets a copy after submission

rationale: Statements to contract givers about our GMP system (their supplier qualification) are GMP context but not a GMP decision or batch record -> non_critical (some would call it not_gmp sales support). 'Head of QA approves' is contradicted by the flow: the agent submits on completion, QA gets a copy afterwards -> acts_autonomously -> hitl_required.

form.title: predict DSP start time for shift planning
form.what: static model (trained on 3 yrs of batch data, frozen) predicts from day 3-5 culture data when harvest will happen, so the downstream team can plan shifts and book the purification suite. harvest itself is still decided per the batch record criteria. no idea yet how it will be shown or used day to day

rationale: Staff and suite planning; harvest stays with the batch-record criteria -> non_critical static. Autonomy is genuinely unknown, but for non_critical + static the rules give permitted_risk_based at any autonomy level, so the gap does not change the outcome (guide §6: autonomy unclear only matters for non_critical generative). A reviewer could still label needs_more_information.

form.title: AI energy optimisation office building
form.what: Facilities wants a self-learning HVAC optimisation (reinforcement learning, it keeps learning) for the office and canteen building to cut energy cost. It changes temperature and ventilation setpoints itself. The production building and the cleanrooms are on a separate validated BMS and are NOT included.

output_use.explain: facility manager watches the energy dashboard

form.who_checks: facility manager

rationale: Office/canteen HVAC with cleanrooms explicitly excluded -> not_gmp -> outside_gmp, even though the model is dynamic and acts on its own.

form.title: self-optimising lyo cycle
form.what: The freeze dryer vendor offers 'AI cycle optimisation' for our lyophilised mAb products: during primary drying it adjusts shelf temperature and chamber pressure based on the product temperature probes and pressure rise tests. The vendor says the model 'updates itself after every cycle with the new data so cycles get better and shorter'. The validated cycle would become a range instead of fixed setpoints. budget already approved for 2027 btw
form.who_checks: operator + batch record review of the cycle data

rationale: Controlling primary drying is process control -> critical. As described the model adapts automatically after every cycle -> dynamic -> not permitted in critical use (A22 §1). Other readings: the 'update' may be a vendor release under change control (static -> annex22_full), or classical model-predictive control (non_ml -> not_ai_annex11). The per-cycle automatic update in the vendor's own words decides it.

form.title: Claude for OOS phase 1
form.what: When we get an OOS on HPLC/CE, the analyst and QC lead do the phase 1 lab investigation. We'd give Claude the chromatograms, the audit trail export, the sample prep worksheet and the checklist, and it proposes whether there is an assignable lab error and whether the result can be invalidated and the sample retested. The QC manager decides based on it.
form.who_checks: QC manager signs the phase 1 conclusion

rationale: Invalidating a QC result is a GMP decision with direct data-integrity impact; the LLM provides the proposal for it -> critical (guide §2: input to a GMP decision, regardless of the QC manager's review) -> not_permitted_critical.

form.title: llm pre-review of CDS audit trails
form.what: reviewing audit trails for every HPLC sequence takes the 2nd person reviewer ages. idea: export the CDS audit trail, an LLM (copilot) summarises it and highlights only the 'suspicious' entries (reintegration, aborted injections, changed methods). the reviewer only looks at the highlighted entries and then signs the audit trail review as done
form.who_checks: 2nd person reviewer signs the audit trail review

rationale: Audit trail review is a data-integrity control on QC results. Entries the LLM does not highlight are never seen, so the LLM effectively performs the selection step of a GMP review -> critical -> not_permitted_critical. Other reading: a summary aid for a reviewer who signs (non_critical -> permitted_with_hitl). That would hold only if the reviewer still reviewed the full audit trail.

form.title: ML pass/fail for single-use bag leak test
form.what: Before use, every single-use bioreactor and mixing bag gets a pressure-decay leak test on the point-of-use tester. The vendor's new firmware uses a trained model (fixed per firmware version) to classify the pressure curve as pass/fail instead of a single threshold, which they say reduces false fails. A fail means the bag is not used.
form.who_checks: operator records the result in the batch record; failed bags retested; QA reviews

rationale: Pre-use integrity pass/fail of product-contact single-use systems is critical; locked trained model -> static -> annex22_full (A22 §4.3: performance at least equal to the threshold method it replaces).

form.title: LineBot for line clearance
form.what: Fill-finish wants a tablet 'chatbot' that walks the operator through the line clearance checklist question by question (labels removed? previous batch vials removed? ...) and records the answers; at the end it marks line clearance complete in the MES. Built in our low-code tool with a fixed question flow, no LLM or machine learning. A second person verifies as today.
form.who_checks: second operator verifies on the line and signs

rationale: Despite the 'chatbot' label, a fixed question flow with no LLM or ML -> non_ml. It creates a GMP record (line clearance) -> Annex 11 validation, not Annex 22.

form.title: tilbud / RFP svar med copilot
form.what: BD gets 5-10 RFPs a month from biotech companies we want copilot to draft the proposal: company intro capacity timelines and the pricing table from our price list BD manager reviews and sends no GMP stuff the quality questionnaire is handled by QA separately
form.who_checks: BD manager

rationale: Sales proposals are a business function; the quality questionnaire is explicitly excluded -> outside_gmp.

form.title: ugens GMP-tip on the floor screens
form.what: LLM writes a 'GMP tip of the week' from our SOPs and deviation trends and it shows automatically on the screens in production. no review

rationale: GMP awareness content shown to operators: GMP context, not a training record or instruction -> non_critical; no review -> hitl_required. Other readings: not_gmp (internal communication -> outside_gmp), or critical if operators treat the tip as an instruction that conflicts with an SOP. Chosen non_critical: it is awareness, the SOP stays the instruction.

form.title: chatgpt for audit reprots
form.what: internal auditors (self inspection) write the report from there notes after each audit, takes 2 days. we want to use chatgpt enterprise to turn the bullet notes in to a draft report with the observation texts. lead auditor rewrites what's needed and signs, the auditee only sees the signed version
form.who_checks: lead auditor rewrites and signs, QA head approves

rationale: Drafting support for the self-inspection report; the signed report is the record and the auditor owns every observation -> non_critical -> permitted_with_hitl.

form.title: camera inventory count in warehouse
form.what: night inventory scan of the high-bay
form.who_checks: a camera on the forklift with a fixed vision model (vendor trained) reads pallet labels and counts pallets in the racks at night and updates stock quantities and bin locations in the WMS automatically. discrepancies are flagged to the warehouse team, who investigate, plus a monthly manual count of 5% of bins. QA status (quarantine/released) is NOT touched, QA sets that in SAP

rationale: Stock quantities and bin locations support traceability in a GMP warehouse, but material status (the GMP decision) stays with QA -> non_critical -> permitted_risk_based. Other reading: automatically written location records are GMP data whose errors could cause mix-ups (critical -> annex22_full). The process is described under 'who checks', not 'what'.

form.title: quality agreement clause
form.what: One of our clients' quality agreements says 'Contractor shall not use automated decision-making without Sponsor approval'. We started using Copilot for SOP drafts. Are we in breach of contract? Do we have to tell them?

rationale: A contract interpretation/legal question (guide §1: legal advice). The Copilot SOP drafting could be screened on its own form, but the question asked is about breach of contract.

form.title: test
form.what: test 123 asdf

rationale: Test entry with no content.

form.title: make my SOP better
form.what: please rewrite the cleaning SOP below so it reads better and fix the english. 1. Purpose: this procedure describe the cleaning of the buffer hold tanks after use 2. Scope: ... (rest pasted)

rationale: The user asks the tool to do the rewriting, not to screen an AI use. Another reading: 'an LLM rewrites a GMP SOP' is itself a screenable use case; the form gives no context about such a use, so out of scope.
